question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [English Naval Victories and their Locations]
options: Defeat of the Spanish Armada — English Channel and North Sea, 1588
Battle of Trafalgar — Cape Trafalgar, off southwest Spain, 1805
Battle of Lagos — off the coast of Portugal, 1759
Battle of the Nile — Bay of Biscay, 1798
wrong_fact: The Battle of the Nile (1798) was fought in Aboukir Bay (near Alexandria), Egypt — NOT in the Bay of Biscay. It was Nelson's crushing defeat of the French fleet that stranded Napoleon's army in Egypt.
explanation: The Spanish Armada was defeated in 1588 as it sailed through the English Channel, with storms in the North Sea completing its destruction. The Battle of Trafalgar (1805) was fought off Cape Trafalgar on Spain's Atlantic coast, where Nelson defeated the Franco-Spanish fleet. The Battle of Lagos (1759) was fought off Portugal's Algarve coast, a British victory over the French. However, the Battle of the Nile (August 1798) was fought in Aboukir Bay near Alexandria, Egypt — Nelson destroyed Brueys' French fleet, stranding Napoleon's army in Egypt.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [English East India Company Naval Bases in India and their Coasts]
options: Surat factory — Gujarat coast (western India), first English factory in India
Madras (Fort St. George) — Coromandel Coast (southeastern India)
Bombay — Konkan coast, transferred from Portuguese to English as dowry (1661)
Calcutta (Fort William) — Malabar Coast, founded by Job Charnock (1690)
wrong_fact: Calcutta (Fort William) was founded on the Hooghly River in Bengal (eastern India), NOT on the Malabar Coast. The Malabar Coast is on India's southwest (modern Kerala).
explanation: Surat was the first English trading post in India (established 1608/1613) on the Gujarat coast. Fort St. George, Madras was established in 1639 on the Coromandel Coast. Bombay was given to England as part of the dowry for Catherine of Braganza's marriage to Charles II in 1661, on the Konkan coast. Calcutta was founded by Job Charnock in 1690 on the Hooghly River in Bengal — far away on the eastern coast, not the Malabar Coast which lies in present-day Kerala.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Anglo-French Naval Conflicts in India and their Locations]
options: Battle of Sadras — off Coromandel Coast near Sadras, February 1782 (Hughes vs Suffren)
Battle of Providien — off eastern Sri Lanka coast, April 1782
Battle of Trincomalee — off eastern Sri Lanka coast, September 1782
Battle of Cuddalore — off Bengal coast near Calcutta, June 1783
wrong_fact: The Battle of Cuddalore (June 1783) was fought off Cuddalore on the Coromandel Coast of southeastern India (Tamil Nadu), NOT off the Bengal coast near Calcutta.
explanation: The series of naval battles between Admiral Hughes (British) and Suffren (French) are well-documented: Sadras (Feb 1782) was fought off the Coromandel Coast near Sadras in Tamil Nadu. Providien (Apr 1782) was fought near Trincomalee off Sri Lanka's east coast. Trincomalee (Sep 1782) was another engagement in the same region. However, the Battle of Cuddalore (June 1783) — the final and decisive battle of this series — was fought off Cuddalore in Tamil Nadu on the Coromandel Coast, not near Calcutta or Bengal.
